title: Frame phase retrievability and state distinguishability of quantum channels
abstract: This survey introduces the role of frame phase retrieval in pure-state identification and information preservation by quantum channels. For unit vectors, the lift $x\mapsto xx^*$ identifies vectors that differ only by a global phase with the same rank-one quantum state, converts frame intensities into linear functionals of the lifted state, and makes the adjoint pullback of output observables an operator-valued measurement on the input system. From this viewpoint, a channel is phase retrievable exactly when it is injective on pure states. We develop this correspondence through Choi-rank-two linear combinations of Kraus operators, higher-rank relative spectra, structural obstructions, and constructions with prescribed Choi rank. We distinguish injective identification from full tomography, perfect one-shot discrimination, zero-error classical communication, and exact quantum correction. Twirling channels then provide a structured setting in which commutants, irreducible dimensions, multiplicities, orbit-frame orthogonality, coding indices, and phase-retrievable subspaces can be read from group representations.
summary: This survey characterizes phase retrievability for quantum channels, determining when the output measurement can uniquely distinguish all pure input states. It establishes that this property is equivalent to the channel being injective on pure states, developing advanced mathematical criteria using frame theory and channel decomposition to quantify this information preservation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the conditions under which a quantum channel can retain enough information to uniquely identify pure input quantum states, a concept termed 'phase retrievability'.
main_result: A quantum channel is phase retrievable if and only if it is injective when restricted to the set of pure states. The authors develop quantitative criteria, such as the index $\eta_2(\Phi; M)$, to characterize this property.
method: The analysis combines concepts from frame theory (phase retrieval from intensities) with quantum information theory, utilizing the adjoint channel ($\Phi^*$) and structural criteria involving Choi ranks and relative spectra.
model_or_system: The study focuses on general quantum channels $\Phi: B(HA) 	o B(HB)$ acting on systems described by density matrices or unit vectors in Hilbert spaces. Specific examples include depolarizing or amplitude damping channels.
key_observables: Phase retrievability index ($	ext{pr}(\Phi)$), the measure $\eta_2(\Phi; M)$, and the injectivity of the channel on pure states.
important_parameters: The dimension of the input/output spaces, the structure of the Kraus operators $\{A_i\}$, and the number of uses ($q$) for twirling channels.
main_assumptions: The analysis often distinguishes between 'injective identification' (phase retrievability) and stronger concepts like full tomography or perfect one-shot discrimination.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the structure implies theorems and criteria are presented, likely involving diagrams or mathematical derivations related to channel decomposition and frame properties.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from general phase retrieval concepts for vectors to the application of these ideas to quantum channels. It develops necessary and sufficient conditions using various mathematical tools (Choi rank, spectra) and concludes by applying these findings to structured channels like twirling channels.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to quantify how much information a quantum process (channel) loses, which is fundamental for understanding quantum error correction, quantum communication capacity, and the limits of quantum state estimation.
